sampling_model.design: Independent observational sampling from one fixed mixed-noise law \(P_X\).
sampling_model.treatment: The coordinate \(T\) is intervened upon in each compatible linear structural model; no treatment assignment is randomized in the observed sample.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; stability is supplied by \(\lambda I\preceq\Gamma\preceq\Lambda I\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Source scales are normalized to unit variance before imposing \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le A_{\max}\), with full-column-rank, sign, and lexicographic loading conventions. The explicitly maintained greatest Gaussian-divisor covariance is recovered from centered empirical characteristic-function moduli on coordinate and pair-sum rays; the uniformly quantified literal-Laplace subclass instead uses clipped fourth cumulants and a global Lipschitz modulus.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under Assumptions 2--4 and \(1\le k\le p\), Theorems 2--3 give at most \(p!\) equivalent mixed-noise SCMs and uniqueness once the causal order is known.
Theorems 5--6 give matching logarithmic minimax rates for latent Gaussian covariance estimation under nonparametric contamination.
The paper gives scalar centered Fourier variance estimation and least-favorable unknown-Gaussian-variance pairs under fixed smoothness envelopes.
The paper constructs test-inversion confidence regions for total effects under structure uncertainty and equal error variances.
The paper gives generic total-effect identification and rigorous confidence regions under structure uncertainty using partial equality restrictions on structural-error variances.
Algorithm 3 unions adjustment-set intervals over retained orders; Lemma 1 gives asymptotic coverage of one effect from order-set and conditional-interval validity.
The paper adapts IDA and joint IDA to maximal PDAGs with background knowledge.
The paper derives estimating equations and asymptotic distributions for fourth-moment ICA procedures.
The paper constructs multiplier-bootstrap uniform deconvolution bands with an unknown error law and an auxiliary error sample.

body.tldr: Under mutually independent, unit-variance, nonconstant Gaussian-indecomposable latent sources, a full-column-rank identified loading convention, and an explicit greatest-Gaussian-divisor condition, a known partial order leaves a finite Cholesky-effect fiber. The note represents that fiber by treatment-predecessor ideals and maps a measurable finite-sample characteristic-function covariance region into simultaneous coverage of every compatible effect, including exact collisions. Expected covariance and Hausdorff errors are of order \(1/\log N\) on the fixed ordinary-smooth Fourier class. An explicit positive smooth Laplace--Student splice attains matching covariance, singleton-effect, and honest-diameter lower bounds there; because this fixed class is contained in the Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi Assumptions 2--4 class, the three lower bounds also transfer to that published class and to every superclass containing the fixed splice class. No logarithmic upper bound is claimed for the broader published class. Literal standardized-Laplace sources form a root-\(N\) fourth-cumulant boundary.

project_justification.gap: Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi give finite population identification for mixed-noise models under their Assumptions 2--4, while Belomestny--Trabs--Tsybakov treat Fourier covariance recovery and Wang--Kolar--Drton propagate order uncertainty to one effect in a causally sufficient additive-error setting. These results do not provide a finite-sample event covering every partial-order-compatible Cholesky effect after greatest-Gaussian-divisor recovery, nor the exact-collision confidence-diameter lower bound proved here.
project_justification.niche: The upper and lower questions require different scopes. Honest finite-sample regions and matching rates are established on a fixed-dimensional class with known ordinary-smooth ray envelopes and compact spectral, loading, and moment bounds; the explicit lower witnesses additionally satisfy the broader Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi published source hypotheses.
project_justification.fill: The note supplies the predecessor-ideal functional, an explicit centered ray region with polarization, spectral clipping, and bounded fallback, finite-sample simultaneous whole-fiber coverage, a verified smooth splice with vanishing product total variation, matching logarithmic upper and lower rates on the fixed Fourier class, and lower-only covariance, causal-fiber, and honest-diameter transfer to the published class and every superclass containing the fixed splice class.

body.related_work: Sanjaroonpouri and Ramazi are the population-identification anchor. Their Assumptions 2--4 use mutually independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources with no Gaussian component, \(1\le k\le p\), unit covariance normalization, lexicographically ordered reduced-loading columns, and full column rank. The fixed exponent-two Fourier class used here satisfies those hypotheses, while adding known Fourier envelopes and compact spectral, loading, and moment restrictions for uniform inference. The explicit splice witnesses therefore transfer logarithmic lower bounds to the published class, but the extra restrictions are essential to the upper proof and no upper rate over the full published class is asserted. The greatest-Gaussian-divisor condition remains explicit in the Fourier model and is verified directly for the witnesses. Belomestny, Trabs, and Tsybakov supply the multivariate characteristic-function polarization precedent, and Meister supplies the scalar fixed-envelope centering and compensated lower-pair architecture; the present proof verifies the six-degree positivity, uniform derivatives, weighted Parseval bound, and causal collision embedding. Wang, Kolar, and Drton study recursive causally sufficient additive-error models and asymptotic coverage of one effect after order and adjustment-set inference; no blanket inclusion relation between their full model and the present one is used. Perkovi\'c, Kalisch, and Maathuis connect background knowledge to IDA effect multisets, while the CRAN \(\texttt{pcalg::ida}\) and Maathuis et al. yeast intervention-ranking workflow motivate reporting an honest compatible-effect set under an audited mixed-noise/Fourier model rather than a selected Gaussian-causal-sufficiency list. Miettinen, Taskinen, Nordhausen, and Oja provide the fourth-cumulant estimating-equation precedent for the literal-Laplace boundary.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The logarithmic upper guarantee is uniform only with fixed dimension and known ray exponents, Fourier envelopes, spectral bounds, loading bound, and eighth-moment bound. The lower splice uses a fixed three-variable exponent-two class and conservative numerical constants; its independently checked derivative and weighted-Parseval estimates establish the claimed product indistinguishability but do not provide adaptation to unknown smoothness or a matching upper theorem over the unrestricted Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi class.
body.honest_scope: The theorem-level deliverables are the exact ideal representation, collision-stable Lipschitz transfer, measurable finite-sample covariance and whole-fiber regions, \(O((\log N)^{-1})\) expected error on the fixed Fourier class, the explicit positive smooth-splice pair, matching fixed-class minimax and honest-diameter results, lower-only transfer to the Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi class and every superclass containing the fixed splice class, and the uniformly quantified literal-Laplace boundary. No blanket nonnestedness theorem is claimed. The broader published class receives no upper-rate claim because it does not impose the uniform Fourier envelopes or compact spectral, loading, and moment bounds used by the estimator analysis. The proposal also does not claim adaptation to unknown exponents, growing-dimension guarantees, polynomial-delay ideal enumeration, correct singleton selection, or minimax sharpness for every exponent profile. When the partial order is total, the ideal family has one treatment-predecessor set and the fiber reduces to the usual singleton regression effect.
